Variants.Content: Entry The Long Night is Westeros' oldest and most difficult-to-prove catastrophic legend: darkness and cold envelope the world, the dead rest no sleep, the last hero travels across the wilderness in search of the Children of the Forest, and the dawn battle finally dispels the darkness. Bran the Builder is believed to have built the Wall with Maesters question the precise dates, characters, and magic of eight thousand years ago, while northerners regard each unusually cold winter as a reminder that the story may be approaching again. The Long Night is first and foremost a memory of shared fear, explaining why the Wall, Night's Watch, and the Old Gods of the North are so heavy in the history of the Seven Kingdoms.
